entries.reason: a typed array is a value of the engine, not a function this port could wrap: the release's JavaScriptCore has neither ArrayBuffer nor TypedArray, so there is nothing to read a buffer out of and nothing to make one over. Measured three ways: the release's C API exports no typed-array entry point (tools/cache-index/first-rung.py answers 10.0.1, the oldest held rung carrying the name, for all thirteen of these); the 6.1.3 armv7 cache's own symbol table carries 300 JSC:: symbols, JSC::JSArray and JSC::JSString among them, and none for JSC::JSArrayBuffer or JSC::JSTypedArray; and the SDK's own JSTypedArray.h dates every one of the thirteen at ios(10.0). Carrying them would mean a different engine, not a wrapper - see facts/JavaScriptCore/CAPI.md
entries.effect: the function is not there: a weak reference to it is NULL. No value on this release is a typed array or an ArrayBuffer, so the answer the function exists to give - a buffer, a length, an offset, a type - has no value to give it about, and a client that reached it would be reading 0 out of nothing
